propositions: External and live-service CI pytest lanes lack per-test hang guards while the shared suite (_build-and-test.yml) carries --timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread, allowing deadlocked tests to hide with no traceback or culprit identification.

Eight unguarded pytest lanes (six discovered in triage, two in _eval-discipline and _optionality) need calibrated per-test timeout budgets based on observed historical mean test duration, floored at 300s and capped at 10x mean per lane.

The parity detection rule in test_ci_workflow_parity.py must exhaustively sweep all .github/workflows files and assert both --timeout= and --timeout-method=thread flags on every pytest invocation, catching all four command forms (pytest -m, bare pytest <path>, python -m pytest, path-prefixed python -m pytest) while excluding non-invoking text and comments.

Live-service lanes (external-llm with 900s, external with 600s, jira-dc-harness with 900s) and single-test sweeps (structured-output-baseline with 3600s) require variance allowances beyond the 10x-mean rule to accommodate legitimate bedrock/field-readiness variance and deliberate human-dispatched sweep sizes.
The _optionality.yml degradation-path step runs in a minimal /tmp/clean venv and must explicitly install pytest-timeout alongside pytest and jsonschema to honor the timeout flag without erroring.
